name: Eiffel Tower
overview: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower and global cultural icon of France. Standing 330 meters tall, it was the world's tallest man-made structure until 1930 and remains one of the most visited monuments in the world.
history: Built for the 1889 World's Fair celebrating the French Revolution's centenary, this 'Iron Lady' was initially despised by Parisians who called it a 'metal asparagus' and 'eyesore.' Writers like Guy de Maupassant ate lunch at its restaurant daily because it was the only place in Paris where he couldn't see the tower! Designed by Gustave Eiffel in just 2 years, it was meant to be temporary and nearly demolished in 1909. Instead, it became a radio transmission tower, saving it from destruction. During WWII, the French Resistance cut the elevator cables, forcing Nazis to climb 1,665 steps to hang their flag. Hitler ordered its destruction during the Liberation of Paris, but the German commander refused. Today, it's the most-visited paid monument in the world and the ultimate symbol of love, receiving countless marriage proposals daily.
highlights: Three observation levels with different perspectives
Summit access via elevator to 276 meters
Trocadéro viewing area for classic tower photos
Hourly light show after sunset (5 minutes)
tips: Book timed entry tickets online to avoid long queues. Visit at sunset for day and night views. The hourly sparkle show happens for 5 minutes every hour after dark. Restaurants on first and second floors require separate reservations.
